issues.description: Accessor visibility for Animal.name differs between problem statement and solution. The problem statement/UML specifies that the name getter and setter on class Animal should be protected (UML shows protected '#' for getName() and setName(), and the textual note instructs to implement the name getter and setter with protected visibility). The solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) declares these methods as public (getName() at line 10 and setName(...) at line 14). This mismatch can confuse students about the intended encapsulation and inheritance design and could cause grading or automated checks to flag correct-looking code as inconsistent with the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the specification by changing the access modifiers in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java: change the getter signature from 'public String getName()' to 'protected String getName()' (line 10) and the setter from 'public void setName(String newName)' to 'protected void setName(String newName)' (line 14). Alternatively, if public accessors are intended, update the UML and the textual note in problem_statement.md to state that getName() and setName(...) are public.

issues.description: Constructor visibility for class Animal differs between problem statement and solution. The UML in the problem statement marks the Animal(String) constructor as protected (the UML uses '#' to indicate protected visibility). The solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) declares the constructor as public (public Animal(String name) at line 6). This inconsistency may confuse students about intended instantiation rules for the abstract base class and about inheritance/visibility expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Animal constructor protected in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java by changing 'public Animal(String name)' to 'protected Animal(String name)' (line 6) to match the UML and the problem text. If the intent is to allow a public constructor, update the UML/description in problem_statement.md to reflect that the Animal constructor is public.
